title: Tale of the Lover Who Feigned Himself a Thief (Español)

keywords: tale of the lover who feigned himself a thief
full_text:
In the city of Basra lived a noble young man named Wafiq who was deeply in love with the daughter of an affluent neighbor. Their affection was pure and mutually shared, but her strict father had forbidden any communication between them.

One starlit evening, driven by longing, Wafiq climbed the outer garden wall merely to catch a glimpse of her walking among the rosebushes. As he peered down from the parapet, the watchmen of the city happened to patrol the alley. Seeing a young man climbing the wall of a wealthy merchant's home, the guards shouted: 'A thief! Catch the burglar!' and seized him.

Wafiq realized his dilemma: if he spoke the truth and explained his presence, he would save himself from punishment, but the innocent maiden's reputation would be tarnished forever across the gossip of the bazaars. If he remained silent or claimed to be a thief, he faced the executioner's scimitar.

Choosing chivalric honor over self-preservation, Wafiq held his tongue and confessed before the magistrate: 'I climbed the wall to steal the merchant’s gold. Punish me as the law decrees.'

The magistrate sentenced him to have his right hand severed in the public square. On the appointed morning, as the executioner raised the blade, a veiled lady rushed through the crowd, crying: 'Hold your hand, O judge! This man is no thief!'

The maiden threw herself before the magistrate and revealed the noble truth: 'He climbed the wall out of pure love for me, and confessed to a crime he never committed to shield my name from scandal! If anyone must be punished, punish me, but do not harm the noblest soul in Basra!'

The magistrate, the merchant, and all the citizens were moved to tears by such heroic chivalry and mutual fidelity. The merchant embraced the young man, granted him his daughter’s hand in marriage with a handsome dowry, and praised the courage that had chosen honor over life itself.
moral: Selfless chivalry that risks one's own life to protect another's honor is ultimately vindicated by truth. [ES]
